title: CJK horizontal, vertical, and ruby layout
stressor: CJK horizontal and vertical writing modes, ruby annotations

fonts.source: Noto Sans CJK JP (NotoSansCJK-VF.otf.ttc, face 0), variable font instanced at wght=400, then subset to only the glyphs used on this page with fontTools pyftsubset

notes: Original Japanese and Simplified Chinese sentences authored for this fixture. Designed for 960x640, white background, dark text. Three CJK blocks: a horizontal Japanese paragraph (default writing-mode), a vertical Japanese block (writing-mode: vertical-rl, right-to-left flow), and a ruby line with <rt> furigana over kanji, plus a short Simplified Chinese line for Han coverage. English <h1>/<h2> headings label each block. The embedded NyalaCJK webfont is a subset of Noto Sans CJK JP covering every CJK and kana glyph on the page, so headless Chromium renders real glyphs rather than tofu without relying on a system CJK font. CSS is inline, the font is base64 @font-face, and there are no external URLs, no <script>, and no @import. Verified by capture: screenshot.png shows correct CJK glyphs, vertical-rl flow, and ruby furigana, with no tofu boxes.

placement_gate.reason: CJK vertical and ruby runs fall back off the embedded face, so advances differ from 2*cellW. Ruby padding keeps annotations off the base row. Repeated corpus runs at all three geometries leave two collisions between neighbouring base runs, so the collision limit is 2. The drift limits still cover the fallback font advances.
